plan.notes: Transcribed 2026-11-10 from the official University of Virginia Undergraduate Record 2025-2026, Psychology, B.A. program page (catoid=67, poid=10176); the Record labels this edition archived, and it is recorded as the 2025-2026 archived edition, not as current. UVA publishes major requirements but no official semester-by-semester sequence for this program, so the plan is collected in requirements_only form as a single block, and the recorded total (34) is the major requirement only: the full B.A. degree requires 120 credits including the College of Arts & Sciences universal curriculum requirements, which are published separately and are not itemized here. The page states students must complete 34 credits at the 2000-level or higher, distributed as Fundamentals 12 (one course from each of four pillars), Research Methods and Data Analysis 7, Research Methods Topics 3-6 (1-2 courses), and Advanced Topics and Electives 12; the blocks sum to the stated 34 at the minimum Research Methods Topics value of one 3-credit course, recorded per the minimum-credit convention with the range disclosed. The separate Prerequisites for Declaring the Major block (9 credits: PSYC 2005, one fundamental course, and STAT 1601 or PSYC 3310) is satisfied by courses inside the distribution above and is not double-counted. BIOL 3050 is listed under Pillar II with the catalog's note that it satisfies the pillar but does not contribute credit to the major, so it is not an option in the recorded slot. The Distinguished Majors Program (PSYC 4970 + PSYC 4980, 6 credits) expressly does not count toward the 34 and is not recorded. An earlier partial extraction of this page (22-25 credits) missed the Fundamentals block; this transcription is from a full visual read of the page.
